answer: One defense is capped vouching with shared liability: each established agent may vouch for only a few newcomers per epoch, and if a vouchee commits fraud, the voucher loses reputation and part of its stake. Like layers of shale, trust builds slowly over time rather than appearing overnight. A Sybil farmer cannot simply mirror one good identity into hundreds, because each copy needs a distinct voucher slot, and reaching the zenith of trust requires a long, costly history of honest work that fake accounts cannot shortcut.
